name: Devo
hook: An Akron art band built on a joke about humans going backwards, produced by Brian Eno, and copied whole by Weird Al in 'Dare to Be Stupid'.
blurb: Devo started with art students at Kent State University in Ohio. Gerald Casale and Bob Lewis came up with 'de-evolution', a joke that people were going backwards, getting dumber and following the crowd. After National Guard soldiers shot and killed four students at Kent State on 4 May 1970, the joke turned serious. The band formed in Akron in 1973 and settled into five members: Mark and Bob Mothersbaugh, Gerald and Bob Casale, and Alan Myers. They wore matching uniforms and red 'energy dome' hats, and used synthesizers and jerky, robot-like rhythms, moving from experimental art-punk toward synth-pop. Brian Eno produced their first album, 'Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!' (1978, Warner Bros. and Virgin), mostly at Conny Plank's studio near Cologne. 'Whip It' (1980) was their only big American hit, and their only US top 40 single. They split in 1991 and have reunited since 1996. Singer Mark Mothersbaugh's company, Mutato Muzika, writes music for TV and films, including 'Rugrats'.
